description:

By analyzing this data, stakeholders can identify schools that excel or need improvement, ultimately contributing to lifelong learning initiatives and enhancing educational strategies in the region.

It includes key metrics such as total days present, total days absent, and attendance percentages, allowing for detailed analysis of student attendance patterns. The dataset features 15 unique grade levels and spans five academic years, with a total of 29,748 unique values for total days recorded. Each entry captures essential information, including the number of days students were present and absent, as well as the percentage of students classified as chronically absent. This data can be utilized by educators, policymakers, and researchers to identify trends in student attendance, assess the impact of absenteeism on academic performance, and develop targeted interventions to improve student engagement and attendance rates. description:
This dataset provides comprehensive information on various educational institutions and community facilities across New York City, focusing on their accessibility and meal options. It includes key details such as district, school name, site address, city, zip code, and geographic coordinates (longitude and latitude). The dataset categorizes accessibility into three types: no accessibility, partially accessible, and fully accessible, allowing users to assess the mobility options available at each location. Additionally, it specifies that all meal types listed are non-kosher, which is crucial for understanding dietary options. With 32 unique districts and 332 unique school codes, this dataset serves as a valuable resource for analyzing free meal distribution programs, identifying areas in need of improved accessibility, and supporting community outreach efforts aimed at enhancing educational and nutritional support for students and families in the city.

district: integer; required  
sfcode: string; nullable  
bldgcode: string; nullable  
schoolname: string; required  
siteaddress: string; required  
city: string; required  
zip: string; required; format: 5-digit postal code  
accessibility: enumerated values: {No Accessibility, Fully Accessible, Partially Accessible}; required  
longitude: float; range: -180 to 180  
latitude: float; range: -90 to 90  
koshermealtype: enumerated values: {kosher, non-kosher}; required

description:
This dataset provides detailed school attendance data, capturing key metrics such as enrollment, attendance, and absences across various schools over multiple academic years, specifically from 2018-2019 to 2020-2021. It includes 1,608 unique school identifiers and records attendance data for 476 distinct dates, allowing for comprehensive analysis of student presence and engagement. The dataset features several important columns: 'enrolled' indicates the number of students enrolled on a given day, 'present' counts those attending school, 'absent' tracks those not present, and 'released' notes students who were released for any reason. This data can be instrumental for educational researchers, policymakers, and school administrators to assess attendance trends, identify areas for improvement, and develop strategies to enhance student engagement and retention. The temporal coverage of the dataset, with daily resolution, enables detailed longitudinal studies of attendance patterns over time.

Column constraints outlined in Data Dictionary:
school_dbn: format must be a string of 3 letters followed by 3 digits; uniqueness required  
date: format must be a valid date in ISO 8601 or MM/DD/YYYY; null values not allowed  
schoolyear: format must be a string representing a school year in the format YYYYYYYY; null values not allowed  
enrolled: value must be a non-negative integer; null values not allowed  
present: value must be a non-negative integer; null values not allowed  
absent: value must be a non-negative integer; null values not allowed; absent must be less than or equal to enrolled  
released: value must be a non-negative integer; null values not allowed; released must be less than or equal to enrolled

This dataset provides detailed monthly attendance records for various schools, covering multiple academic years. It includes key attributes such as school identification, school year, month, grade level, and attendance counts, allowing for comprehensive analysis of student attendance patterns. The dataset features 1,603 unique schools and spans three academic years, with attendance data categorized by month and grade level, from Pre-Kindergarten to 12th grade. Each entry records the number of students present, absent, and released during the reporting month, facilitating insights into attendance trends and potential areas for improvement. The semantic profile highlights the educational context of the data, emphasizing its utility for measuring student engagement and performance. This dataset can be instrumental for educators, policymakers, and researchers aiming to enhance school attendance strategies and understand the factors influencing student attendance over time.

month_code: 2 digit code; must be between 01 and 12 inclusive  
schoolyear: expressed as Year of the Start of School and Year at the end of school; format YYYY-YY  
gradelevel: allowed values include PK, 0K, and integers from 1 to 12 inclusive; PK and 0K represent specific grades  
gradesort: allowed values include -1 (PK), 0 (0K), and integers from 1 to 12 inclusive; PK is represented by -1 and 0K by 0  
roster_count: non-negative integer; must be greater than or equal to 0  
present: non-negative integer; must be greater than or equal to 0  
absent: non-negative integer; must be greater than or equal to 0  
released: non-negative integer; must be greater than or equal to 0

This dataset contains detailed school attendance records, capturing daily attendance metrics across various schools from the 2015-2016 to the 2016-2017 school years. It includes information on the number of students enrolled, present, absent, and released on specific dates, with a total of 1,639 unique school identifiers and 362 unique dates. The data spans from September 16, 2015, to June 12, 2017, providing a comprehensive view of student attendance patterns. Each entry reflects the number of students present, absent, and released, based on valid attendance submissions, making it a valuable resource for analyzing attendance trends and identifying areas for improvement in student engagement. This dataset can be utilized by educators, policymakers, and researchers to assess school performance, develop strategies to enhance attendance, and support educational initiatives aimed at increasing student participation in schools.

Column constraints outlined in Data Dictionary:
school: must follow the format of a 3-letter borough code followed by a 3-digit school number (e.g., XX000)  
enrolled: must be a non-negative integer; must equal the sum of present, absent, and released  
present: must be a non-negative integer; must be less than or equal to enrolled  
absent: must be a non-negative integer; must be less than or equal to enrolled  
released: must be a non-negative integer; must be less than or equal to enrolled

This dataset provides a comprehensive directory of schools in New York City, specifically focusing on kindergarten admissions. It includes essential information such as the school name, grade span, type of school (zoned, non-zoned, or charter), and accessibility features, which indicate whether a school is fully, partially, or not accessible. The dataset also flags schools that offer Gifted & Talented programs and dual language programs, enhancing its utility for families seeking specialized educational options. With 962 unique school identifiers (DBNs) and detailed geographic coordinates, users can easily locate schools within their communities. This dataset serves as a valuable resource for parents navigating the kindergarten admissions process, providing insights into school offerings and accessibility. Additionally, it includes demographic and geographic data, such as community boards and council districts, which can aid in understanding the educational landscape across different neighborhoods. Overall, this dataset is an essential tool for families and educators alike.

description:
This dataset provides comprehensive information about community schools in New York City, including details such as the school’s unique identification number (dbn), building code (bldg_code), school name, grades served, and the lead community-based organization partner. With 317 unique dbn values and 267 unique building codes, the dataset captures a diverse range of educational institutions, serving various grade levels from elementary to high school. The semantic profile highlights that the dbn represents the location of each school, while the bldg_code serves as an identification marker. The school name identifies the educational organization, and the grades served categorizes the educational levels offered. Additionally, the lead_cbo_partner indicates the contracted community organization associated with each school. This dataset can be utilized for analyzing the distribution and partnerships of community schools across NYC, facilitating research on educational access and community engagement in the region.

dbn: format must be a string of 8 characters, starting with a number followed by a letter and 5 digits  
bldg_code: format must be a string of 3 characters, starting with a letter followed by 2 digits  
school_name: required; must be a string  
grades_served: allowed values include "Elementary", "K-8", "Junior High-Intermediate-Middle", "High school", "Secondary School"  
lead_cbo_partner: allowed values include "TBD - Open RFP", required; may be null

description:
This dataset provides detailed information about physical education spaces across various schools in New York City, categorized by boroughs such as Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, Staten Island, and the Bronx. It includes key attributes like geographical and administrative district codes, building identifiers, and room functions, allowing users to identify and analyze the availability and usage of spaces like gyms, swimming pools, and outdoor yards. The dataset features 21 unique room functions and covers a range of grade levels from pre-kindergarten to high school. It also indicates whether spaces are shared with other schools and if they serve purposes beyond physical education. This comprehensive dataset can be utilized for research on educational facilities, planning for physical education programs, and assessing the adequacy of recreational spaces in schools, making it a valuable resource for educators, policymakers, and urban planners.

borough: allowed values are Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, Staten Island, Bronx  
admin_district: allowed values are 01 - District 1 to 32 - District 32; 75 - District 75 (Special Education - Citywide)  
ats_code: format is alphanumeric with a pattern of 2 letters followed by 3 digits (e.g. K203); may include NULL  
grade_level: allowed values are IN, PK, 0K, 01 to 12, AD; NULL is allowed  
ownership: allowed values are DOE Owned, Tax Levy Lease, No Data

This dataset provides detailed information on class size distribution across various school districts, focusing on different grade levels and program types. It includes data on 32 unique districts, covering grades from kindergarten to eighth grade, and features seven distinct program types such as General Education, Integrated Co-Teaching, and Gifted and Talented. The dataset captures key metrics like class size, number of students, and the number of classes, allowing for comprehensive analysis of educational environments. Each entry indicates the number of students within a grade, providing insights into student distribution and class dynamics. This dataset can be utilized for evaluating educational equity, understanding class size impacts on learning outcomes, and informing policy decisions related to resource allocation in schools. The semantic profile highlights the educational context of the data, emphasizing its relevance for stakeholders interested in improving educational quality and accessibility.

program_type: Allowed values are "Gen Ed", "ICT", "G&T", "SC", "Acc"; "Gen Ed" is defined as classes not coded as special education, integrated co-teaching, gifted and talented, or accelerated; "G&T" classes are for grades K-5; "ICT" classes consist of one general education teacher and one special education teacher; "SC" classrooms have specific student/teacher/paraprofessional ratios; "Acc" courses are high school credit-bearing for middle school students.

This dataset provides comprehensive information on school locations within New York City for the fiscal year 2017. It includes unique identifiers such as the ATS system code and location code, along with detailed descriptions of each school, including its name, type, and management organization. Additionally, it contains contact information for school principals and administrative details, such as the opening date and status of each school. The spatial data, including coordinates and community district information, allows for geographic analysis of school distribution across the city. This dataset can be utilized for educational planning, resource allocation, and community engagement initiatives, making it a valuable tool for policymakers, researchers, and educators interested in understanding school accessibility and demographics in New York City.

description:
This dataset provides a comprehensive overview of student demographics and enrollment across various administrative districts for multiple school years. It includes key variables such as total enrollment, grade-specific enrollments from pre-kindergarten through grade 12, and demographic breakdowns by gender and race/ethnicity. The dataset covers 35 unique administrative districts, with enrollment figures ranging from 5,092 to 138,648 students. It also includes important indicators such as the percentage of students with disabilities, English language learners, and those facing economic hardship, measured through the Economic Need Index. This dataset can be utilized for analyzing trends in student demographics, assessing educational equity, and informing policy decisions aimed at improving educational outcomes. Additionally, it serves as a valuable resource for researchers and educators seeking to understand the diverse needs of students within the educational system.

Column constraints outlined in Data Dictionary:
administrative_district: Allowed values: 01-32, 75, 79, 84; District 75 includes Special Education schools; District 79 includes Alternative Schools and Programs; District 84 includes charter schools  
year: Range of possible values: 2015-16 through 2019-20  
students_with_disabilities: Defined as any child receiving an Individualized Education Program (IEP) as of the end of the school year (or March 06 for 2019-20)  
poverty: Counts based on the number of students with families who have qualified for free or reduced price lunch, or are eligible for Human Resources Administration (HRA) benefits; In previous years, the poverty indicator also included students enrolled in a Universal Meal School (USM)  
economic_need_index: The Economic Need Index (ENI) estimates the percentage of students facing economic hardship; Calculated as the average of students’ Economic Need Values; ENI values may vary slightly due to differences in timing of data collection; Students missing ENI data are imputed with the average ENI at their school

description:
This dataset provides insights into student discipline trends across various schools, detailing the removals, principal referrals, and expulsions of students categorized by race and ethnicity. It includes a unique identifier for each school (dbn), the school name, and its category, along with the administrative district it belongs to. The dataset captures counts of disciplinary actions for different racial groups, including American Indian/Alaskan Native, Asian, Black, Hispanic, White, Multi-Racial, and those of unknown backgrounds. Each column represents specific metrics, such as the number of students removed from classrooms or referred to principals and superintendents. This information can be utilized by educators, policymakers, and researchers to analyze disciplinary practices, identify trends, and develop strategies aimed at improving student behavior and equity in disciplinary actions across diverse educational settings.

This dataset provides a comprehensive analysis of class sizes across various grade levels in educational settings, specifically focusing on the number of students enrolled and the types of programs offered. It includes data on 10 unique grade levels and 6 program types, such as General Education, Integrated Co-Teaching, and Self-contained Special Education. The dataset captures class sizes ranging from fewer than 6 to over 34 students, with a total of 216 unique enrollment figures. It also details the percentage of students within each grade enrolled in classes, offering insights into educational trends and resource allocation. This information is crucial for educators and policymakers aiming to understand class dynamics and improve educational outcomes. By analyzing this dataset, stakeholders can make informed decisions regarding class size management and program effectiveness, ultimately enhancing the learning environment for students.

program_type: Allowed values are "Gen Ed", "ICT", "SC", "G&T"; Combinations of these values are also allowed (e.g., "Gen Ed/ICT/G&T", "K-8 SC,SC 12:1:1").  
number_of_students: Must be a non-negative integer; Values may include "<15", "< 6", ">15", ">34", and other similar expressions indicating ranges.

description:
This dataset provides detailed information on meal periods served in various schools across New York City, categorized by borough, geographic district, and city council district. It includes unique identifiers for each school, such as building codes and organization names, along with the type of meal served—either breakfast or lunch—and the number of periods each meal is offered. The dataset features five boroughs, 32 geographic districts, and 51 city council districts, ensuring comprehensive coverage of the city's educational landscape. Each entry is associated with a specific school, allowing for easy identification and analysis. This dataset can be utilized for assessing meal distribution, planning nutritional programs, and understanding the educational environment's impact on student health. It serves as a valuable resource for researchers, policymakers, and educators interested in the intersection of nutrition and education within NYC schools.

Column constraints outlined in Data Dictionary:
borough: Allowed values are K, M, Q, R, X; must be a single character  
geographic_district: Value range is 1 - 32; must be an integer  
city_council_district: Value range is 1 - 51; must be an integer  
meal: Allowed values are Breakfast, Lunch

This dataset provides detailed information about room usage in various educational institutions across New York City. It includes key attributes such as borough, geographic district, city council district, building ID and name, organization ID and name, room number, square footage, whether the room is shared, and the category of the room. The dataset features 5 unique boroughs and 51 city council districts, with a total of 1,350 unique building IDs and 3,868 room numbers. Each room is categorized into types such as Health Clinic, Library, Academic Intervention, and more, allowing for a comprehensive understanding of space utilization. This dataset can be utilized for analyzing room allocation, planning educational resources, and improving facility management within the NYC Department of Education. It serves as a valuable resource for stakeholders interested in optimizing the use of educational spaces and ensuring that facilities meet the needs of students and staff.

description:
This dataset provides comprehensive information on physical education (PE) resources across various schools in New York City, categorized by borough, administrative district, and geographical district. It includes key details such as the school level, student enrollment numbers, and the count of full-time and itinerant licensed PE teachers. The dataset features 1630 unique school identifiers (DBNs) and covers a wide range of student enrollments, from 21 to 5481. Each entry also includes the ratio of full-time licensed PE teachers to students, which is crucial for assessing the availability of PE resources. This dataset can be utilized for analyzing the distribution and adequacy of physical education staffing in schools, helping educators and policymakers identify areas for improvement in PE programs. Additionally, it serves as a valuable resource for research on educational equity and the impact of physical education on student health and well-being.

description:
This dataset provides comprehensive information on physical education resources across various schools in New York City, categorized by borough, administrative district, and geographical district. It includes key details such as school level, student enrollment numbers, and the count of full-time licensed physical education teachers. The dataset features 5 unique boroughs and 33 administrative districts, with student enrollment figures ranging from 64 to 5,838. Each school is identified by a unique location code and district borough number (DBN), facilitating easy aggregation and analysis. The dataset can be utilized to assess the availability and distribution of physical education resources, helping educators and policymakers identify areas for improvement in physical education programs. Additionally, it offers insights into the staffing of physical education teachers, which is crucial for understanding the support provided to students in this essential area of education.

The dataset captures essential metrics, including the number of students, number of classes, and class sizes, allowing for comprehensive analysis of educational environments. Each entry indicates the percentage of students within a grade, offering insights into student distribution and class dynamics. This dataset can be utilized for research on educational equity, resource allocation, and the effectiveness of different teaching programs. It serves as a valuable tool for educators, policymakers, and researchers aiming to understand and improve class size impacts on student learning outcomes.

description: This dataset focuses on pupil transportation issues, specifically tracking various call categories related to transportation incidents and inquiries. description:
This dataset provides comprehensive information on high school graduation rates across various community school districts and city council districts. It includes key details such as the school name, the number of graduates, and the percentage of graduates, allowing for a thorough analysis of educational outcomes. The dataset features 33 unique community school districts and 51 city council districts, with a total of 476 unique school identifiers. Each school is represented by a unique DBN, which combines the school district code, borough code, and a three-digit school number. This data is essential for understanding trends in arts education, as it can be used to evaluate the effectiveness of arts programs in different schools and districts. By analyzing graduation rates, stakeholders can identify successful educational practices and areas needing improvement, ultimately contributing to enhanced educational policies and programs in the arts.

Column constraints outlined in Data Dictionary:
community_school_district: integer; min: 1; max: 75  
city_council_district: integer; min: 1; max: 51  
school_dbn: string; format: "XXYNNN" where X is a digit, Y is a letter, N is a digit; uniqueness required  
school_name: string; required  
number_of_graduates: integer; min: 0  
number_of_graduates_that: integer; min: 0; must be less than or equal to number_of_graduates  
percent_of_graduates_that: decimal; min: 0.0; max: 100.0; format: "X.X%" where X is a digit

description:
This dataset provides insights into student discipline trends across various schools, detailing the number of students removed from classrooms for different durations and the administrative oversight involved. It includes unique identifiers for each school (dbn), the official school names, and their categories, such as elementary or high school. The dataset captures the administrative district for each school, which helps in geographical analysis. Additionally, it records the number of students who experienced removals for varying lengths of time, from one day to 180 days, along with the corresponding principals and superintendents overseeing these cases. This information can be utilized to analyze patterns in student discipline, assess the effectiveness of disciplinary measures, and inform policy decisions aimed at improving student behavior and educational outcomes. Overall, the dataset serves as a valuable resource for educators, policymakers, and researchers interested in understanding and addressing student discipline issues.

description:
This dataset contains the 2010 SAT results for various high schools in New York City, providing valuable insights into student performance across different institutions. It includes key metrics such as the number of test takers, average scores in critical reading, mathematics, and writing, allowing for a comprehensive analysis of academic achievement. Each school is uniquely identified by a code (dbn), and the dataset features 458 unique schools, with the number of test takers ranging from 7 to 1047. The average critical reading scores span from 291 to 674, while mathematics scores range from 281 to 735, and writing scores from 285 to 678. This dataset can be utilized by educators, policymakers, and researchers to evaluate school performance, identify trends in student achievement, and inform strategies for educational improvement. It serves as a crucial resource for understanding the academic landscape of NYC high schools during that year.

Column constraints outlined in Data Dictionary:
dbn: format is a string of 6 characters, starting with a number followed by a letter and 4 digits; uniqueness required  
school_name: non-nullable string; maximum length of 100 characters  
number_of_test_takers: non-nullable numeric; minimum value of 0; maximum value of 804  
critical_reading_mean: numeric; minimum value of 331; maximum value of 674  
mathematics_mean: numeric; minimum value of 346; maximum value of 735  
writing_mean: numeric; minimum value of 336; maximum value of 678

description:
This dataset contains geospatial information on school zones for elementary, middle, and high schools in New York City, specifically focusing on the Department of Education's zoning data. It includes various attributes such as school district numbers, borough identifiers, and unique school identifiers (DBN), which facilitate the identification and categorization of schools. The dataset spans from July 23, 2001, to December 11, 2012, with updates recorded until October 25, 2023. Each entry features a multipolygon geometry representing the boundaries of school zones, allowing for precise mapping and analysis. This data can be utilized for educational planning, policy-making, and community engagement, helping stakeholders understand school zoning dynamics and make informed decisions regarding school placements and resource allocation. The dataset is essential for researchers, educators, and policymakers interested in the intersection of education and urban planning.

Column constraints outlined in Data Dictionary:
the_geom: Multipolygon format; valid geospatial representation
boro_num: Allowed values: M, X, K, Q, R
dbn: Format: XXY### (XX is a district number, Y is a letter code for the borough, ### is a school number)
schooldist: Allowed values: 1 - 32
edit_date: Format: mm/dd/yyyy; Nullable
creat_date: Format: mm/dd/yyyy; Nullable
zoned_dist: Allowed values: 1 - 5
esid_no: Unique internal identifier; Nullable
remarks: Nullable
label: Nullable
shape_leng: Positive numeric value; Units: unspecified
shape_area: Positive numeric value; Units: unspecified

This dataset contains a comprehensive list of active proposals, detailing various services solicited by different departments. Each entry includes a unique solicitation number, the department responsible, a description of the services required, the maximum award amount per contract, the number of contracts to be awarded, and important due dates for proposal submissions. The dataset spans from April 11, 2018, to April 15, 2026, providing a temporal overview of the solicitation process. It features 69 unique solicitation numbers across 29 departments, with a variety of services ranging from building maintenance to IT consulting. The financial data reflects the not-to-exceed award amounts, which vary significantly, indicating the scale of projects. This dataset is essential for firms looking to participate in government contracts, as it provides critical information for preparing proposals and understanding the competitive landscape in public procurement.

solicitation_number: Char(11); required  
due_date: Date; required  
department: Char(50); required  
services: Char(250); required  
not_to_exceed_award_amount_per_contract: Numeric(12,0); required; must be a non-negative value  
number_of_contract_s: Numeric(2,0); required; must be a positive integer  
data_as_of_date: Date; required

It includes information on five distinct program types, such as Student Bathrooms and Lighting Fixture Replacement, across 45 different districts and 614 unique school names. The dataset captures construction start years ranging from 2015 to 2018, providing insights into the timeline of these projects. Each entry includes a description of the work being done, which can range from flood elimination to ADA shelter compliance. The semantic profile highlights key identifiers like program name, district, building ID, and borough, ensuring that users can easily navigate and understand the data. This dataset is valuable for stakeholders interested in tracking school infrastructure improvements, assessing compliance with accessibility standards, and planning future educational facility enhancements.

description:
This dataset provides detailed information on cancelled construction projects within various schools across New York City. It includes key attributes such as district, building ID, school name, borough, program category, and the reason for cancellation. The dataset features 27 unique districts and 5 boroughs, highlighting the geographical distribution of these projects. Each entry is categorized by program type, primarily focusing on upgrades to cafeterias and playgrounds, with reasons for cancellation ranging from prioritization to ineligibility for capital work. The semantic profile indicates that the district and borough fields represent spatial data, while the building ID and school fields serve as identifiers for specific educational institutions. This dataset can be utilized by researchers, policymakers, and educational planners to analyze trends in school construction projects, understand the impact of cancellations, and inform future planning and funding decisions.

district: Required; Format: Numeric string (2 digits)

school: Required; Format: Text  
boro: Required; Allowed values: Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, Staten Island, Bronx

description:
This dataset provides comprehensive information on student vaccination rates across various schools, identified by their unique school DBN codes. It includes data on the number of students over five years old who are actively registered, as well as those who have received at least one dose of vaccination and those who are fully vaccinated. The dataset features a total of 1,584 unique schools, with student counts ranging from 51 to over 823,000. The vaccination data is crucial for understanding public health trends in educational settings, as it highlights the percentage of students vaccinated, which varies significantly across schools. This dataset can be utilized by researchers, policymakers, and public health officials to assess vaccination coverage, identify schools with lower vaccination rates, and develop targeted interventions to improve student health outcomes. Overall, it serves as a valuable resource for analyzing the impact of vaccination programs in the education sector.

description: The i_health_education dataset provides valuable insights into the professional development of health education instructors over a two-year period from 2016 to 2018. The dataset further breaks down attendance into specific session counts, revealing that 403 instructors attended two sessions, while smaller numbers attended three, four, five, or six or more sessions. This dataset is categorized as an educational metric within the healthcare domain, serving as a measurement tool for assessing the engagement of health education instructors in professional development. It can be utilized by educational institutions, policymakers, and researchers to evaluate the effectiveness of training programs and to identify areas for improvement in health education instructor development.
